why: Two- and nine-building checks did not establish whole-map selection behavior. The maximum group exposed repeated membership reconstruction in both map and minimap rendering.
change: Selection filters live identities using one set, then map and minimap each reuse a frame-local membership set. No persistent membership cache or document/history format changes.
fixture: A deterministic no-river 64x64 property with all five authored friends, 256 completed mixed inland buildings, default vegetation, clear arrival area and no authored utility routes. Four trusted Shift-marquees from public minimap views select all buildings, including those outside the initial viewport.
checks: Selection leaves the definition/history unchanged. Copy beyond the published building limit is blocked in preview and actual commit without changing either. One trusted whole-group move compiles, creates one history step, and restores exactly through Undo, Redo and saved reload. Native readiness stays valid. Both runs exited 0 with no page errors and completed cleanup.
observations: Consecutive headless runs using the same verifier and native source: marquee motion p95 44.1 to 6.4 ms; full-group motion p95 64.4 to 7.0 ms; single release 177.1 to 93.4 ms. Motion membership lookups dropped from up to 512/769 for marquee/move to 2/3. Samples include 100 marquee motions and 25 whole-group motions, with only one whole-group release per run.
visual_review: Individually inspected moving-all-buildings.png: the 256-building inspector, whole-group footprints, native ready message and selected minimap remain readable. This intentionally crowded fixture is not a recommended default village or full sprite-art acceptance.
limits: Does not establish physical-display frame pacing, sustained sample distributions, maximum simultaneous nature/routes/history, utility-connected 256-building groups, GPU memory or unfamiliar-player acceptance. Release timings are single observations, not a stable latency percentile.
